data.exact_reserve_text: These losses have been mitigated to some extent by prior year releases which have continued to be a positive part of the Syndicate's result. In 2020 there has been an improvement of GBP 8.2m on closed year reserves, which makes up just over half of the result. On a positive note, the reserves established at last year end in respect of 2017 year of account and prior years have developed favourably during 2020. This has resulted in a release of GBP 8.5m which has improved the overall result.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded a significant gross prior-year release of GBP 91.394m in 2020 (a c.48.3% reduction relative to opening gross claims outstanding of GBP 189.346m), driven principally by favourable claims development and prior-year reserve reviews. This release was reflected in the technical provisions reconciliation and described in the Managing Agent's commentary as prior year releases and improvements on closed year reserves (e.g. releases noted for 2017 and prior). At the same time the 2020 underwriting year experienced a number of named catastrophe losses (Hurricanes Laura, Sally, Delta, Zeta) and pandemic-related impacts which affected current-year underwriting results, but the prior year releases materially offset some of that volatility.

data.data_quality_notes: Primary gross prior-year movement taken from Technical Provisions reconciliation (gross column) = -GBP 91,394k. Narrative references to prior-year improvements (e.g. GBP 8.2m, GBP 8.5m) relate to specific closed years and/or net amounts after reinsurance; where a net figure was the only number given, the gross figure from the technical provisions table was preferred. Claims development triangle is present (gross) and used for cross-checks; RITC activity is noted elsewhere in the report (2018 RITC and RITC receipts) which can distort development patterns for combined years, but the gross prior-year movement used here comes explicitly from the Technical Provisions table. Negative/parentheses values in the statutory tables were preserved (e.g. Marine shown as (698) in notes).
